parts.latex:
The first term of an arithmetic sequence is 5. The sum of the first 43 terms is 2021.

What is the common difference of the sequence?

solutions.latex:
$a = 5,\ S_{43} = 2021$
$$\begin{aligned} \therefore\ 2021 &= \dfrac{43}{2}\big(2\times 5 + (43-1)d\big) \\ 94 &= 10 + 42d \\ d &= 2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes into sum of an arithmetic series formula

parts.latex: Show that a house of cards with 12 rows has a total of 234 cards.

Another house of cards has a total of 828 cards.

How many rows are in this house of cards?

solutions.latex:
Number of cards $= 3 + 6 + 9 + \cdots$ (12 terms)

Arithmetic series
$$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a + (n-1)d\big)$$
with $a = 3$, $d = 3$
$$\begin{aligned} S_{12} &= \dfrac{12}{2}(2 \times 3 + 11 \times 3) \\ &= 234 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the values of $a$ and $d$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $n =$ number of rows.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{n}{2}\big(2 \times 3 + (n-1)3\big) &= 828 \\ n(3n+3) &= 1656 \\ 3n(n+1) &= 1656 \\ n^2 + n &= 552 \\ n^2 + n - 552 &= 0 \\ n &= \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4 \times (-552)}}{2} \\ &= \dfrac{-1 \pm 47}{2} \\ &= 23 \text{ (taking positive solution)} \end{aligned}$$
There are 23 rows.
criteria: Correctly substitutes $a$, $d$ and $828$ into formula for $S_n$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A bricklayer is building a wall in the shape of a triangle where each row contains 3 bricks less than the row immediately below.

The bottom row of the wall contains 150 bricks.

If it takes the bricklayer 10 seconds to install each brick, how many rows of the wall will be completed after 6 hours?

solutions.latex:
In 6 hours the bricklayer lays
$$\dfrac{6\times 60\times 60}{10} = 2160 \text{ bricks}$$
The rows form an arithmetic series with $a = 150$ and $d = -3$:
$$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\big(2\times 150 + (n-1)(-3)\big) = \dfrac{n}{2}(303 - 3n)$$
$$\begin{aligned} S_{17} &= \dfrac{17}{2}(303 - 51) = 2142 \le 2160 \\ S_{18} &= 9(303 - 54) = 2241 > 2160 \end{aligned}$$
So 17 rows are completed.

parts.latex:
Find the simplified exact sum of the arithmetic series
$$\left(\sqrt{3}\right) + \left(2 + \sqrt{3}\right) + \left(4 + \sqrt{3}\right) + \cdots + \left(100 + \sqrt{3}\right)$$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} T_n &= a + (n-1)d \\ 100 + \sqrt{3} &= \sqrt{3} + (n-1)2 \\ n - 1 &= 50 \\ n &= 51 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} S_n &= \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l) \\ &= \dfrac{51}{2}\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{3} + 100\right) \\ &= \dfrac{51}{2}\left(2\sqrt{3} + 100\right) \\ &= 51\left(\sqrt{3} + 50\right) \\ &= 51\sqrt{3} + 2550 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into $S_n$ with $n=51$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: If $x$, $4$ and $y$ are successive terms in an arithmetic sequence and $x$, $3$ and $y$ are successive terms in a geometric sequence, calculate the value of $\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y}$.

solutions.latex:
AP: $4 - x = y - 4$
$$8 = y + x \quad (1)$$
GP:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{3}{x} &= \dfrac{y}{3} \quad (2) \\ 9 &= xy \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y} = \dfrac{x+y}{xy} = \dfrac{8}{9}$$
criteria: Forms both equations $x+y=8$ and $xy=9$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Show that when the blind is raised, the bottom slat rises 540 mm.
How far does the 19th slat rise?
Explain briefly why the distances the slats rise form an arithmetic sequence.

solutions.latex:

$$20(27+2.5)=590$$
When the blind is up:
$$20(2.5)=50$$
$\therefore$ Raised by $590-50=540$ mm.

parts.latex: How many seats are in the first row?
How many seats will this theatre have if there are 9 rows?

solutions.latex:
The number of seats in row $n$ is $T_n=a+(n-1)d$.
$$\begin{aligned} T_3&=a+2d=30\\ T_6&=a+5d=42 \end{aligned}$$
Subtracting, $3d=12$, so $d=4$.
$$\begin{aligned} a&=30-2(4)\\ &=22 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ there are $22$ seats in the first row.

meta.check: Solved simultaneous equations; listed sequence 22, 26, 30, 34, 38, 42 matches T3 and T6.

solutions.latex:
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $a=22$, $d=4$ and $n=9$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_9&=\dfrac{9}{2}\big(2(22)+8(4)\big)\\ &=\dfrac{9}{2}\times 76\\ &=342 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the theatre has $342$ seats.
criteria: Substitutes correctly into a sum formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: There are 25 seats in the front row of an amphitheatre, 30 in the second row, 35 in the 3$^{\text{rd}}$ row and so on such that the number of seats in each row is 5 more than the row in front. How many seats are in the 50$^{\text{th}}$ row?

solutions.latex:
The numbers of seats $25,\ 30,\ 35,\ \ldots$ form an arithmetic sequence with $a=25$ and $d=5$, and the 50th row is $n=50$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_n&=a+(n-1)d\\ T_{50}&=25+(50-1)\times 5\\ &=270\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: The common difference of an arithmetic sequence is $-4$. The sum of the first 30 terms is $23940$ and the sum of the last 30 terms is $-1980$. Find how many terms are in the sequence.

solutions.latex:
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $n=30$ and $d=-4$:
$$\begin{aligned}S_{30}&=\dfrac{30}{2}\big(2a+(30-1)\times(-4)\big)\\23940&=15(2a-116)\\1596&=2a-116\\1712&=2a\\a&=856\end{aligned}$$
Let $n$ be the number of terms. The last 30 terms are
$$a+(n-1)d,\ a+(n-2)d,\ a+(n-3)d,\ \ldots,\ a+(n-30)d$$
and their sum is $-1980$:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Sum}&=a+(n-1)d+a+(n-2)d+a+(n-3)d+\ldots+a+(n-30)d\\&=30a+30dn-d(1+2+3+\ldots+30)\\&=30a+30dn-d\times\dfrac{30}{2}(1+30)\\&=30a+30dn-465d\\-1980&=30\times 856+30\times(-4)n-465(-4)\\-1980&=27540-120n\\120n&=29520\\n&=246\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes a correct simplified expression (algebraic or numeric) for the sum of the last 30 terms, or equivalent merit
Finds the correct value for $a$, or equivalent merit

701.stem: The tenth term of an arithmetic series is 29 and the fifteenth term is 44.

parts.latex: Find the value of the common difference and the value of the first term.
Find the sum of the first 75 terms.

solutions.latex:
Use $T_n=a+(n-1)d$ for the two given terms:
$$\begin{aligned} a+9d&=29 &&\text{(1)}\\ a+14d&=44 &&\text{(2)} \end{aligned}$$
Subtract (1) from (2):
$$\begin{aligned} 5d&=15\\ d&=3 \end{aligned}$$
Substitute $d=3$ into (1):
$$\begin{aligned} a+27&=29\\ a&=2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ a=2,\ d=3$$
criteria: Finds the two equations, or shows some understanding, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Use $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big[2a+(n-1)d\big]$ with $n=75$, $a=2$, $d=3$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{75}&=\dfrac{75}{2}\big(2\times2+(75-1)\times3\big)\\ &=8475 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the sum of the first 75 terms is $8475$.
criteria: Uses the formula for the sum of $n$ terms with one correct value, or equivalent merit

meta.top_criterion_original: Correct answer with working. 1: Uses the formula for the sum of n terms with one correct value.

parts.latex:
Find the sum of the terms in the arithmetic series

$$50+57+64+\cdots+2024.$$

solutions.latex:
The series is arithmetic with
$$a=50, \qquad d=57-50=7$$
The last term, $2024$, is $T_n$:
$$\begin{aligned} T_n=a+(n-1)d &= 2024\\ 50+(n-1)7 &= 2024\\ (n-1)7 &= 1974\\ n-1 &= 282\\ n &= 283\end{aligned}$$
Using the sum formula with first and last terms:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{283} &= \dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)\\ &= \dfrac{283}{2}(50+2024)\\ &= 293\,471\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the value of $n$, or equivalent merit
Finds the correct values of $a$ or $d$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Find the value of the following arithmetic series:

$$1+5+9+\cdots+2025.$$

solutions.latex:
Arithmetic series with $a=1$, $d=4$ and last term $2025$. Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2025&=1+(n-1)\times 4 \\ 2024&=4(n-1) \\ 506&=n-1 \\ n&=507 \end{aligned}$$
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{507}&=\dfrac{507}{2}(1+2025) \\ &=513591 \end{aligned}$$

668.stem:
The formula for the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of a series is given by

$$T_n=400n-2^n$$

parts.latex: What is the sum of the first 10 terms?

solutions.latex:
Split the sum into an arithmetic part and a geometric part:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{10}&=400(1+2+\cdots+10)-(2+2^2+\cdots+2^{10})\\ &=400\times 55-\dfrac{2(2^{10}-1)}{2-1}\\ &=22\,000-2046\\ &=19\,954 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Find the sum of the terms in the arithmetic series:

$$71+64+57+\cdots+(-48)$$

solutions.latex:
$a=71$ and $d=64-71=-7$.

Find the number of terms using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned} -48&=71+(n-1)(-7)\\ -48&=71-7n+7\\ 7n&=126\\ n&=18 \end{aligned}$$
Sum using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$ with last term $l=-48$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{18}&=\dfrac{18}{2}\big(71+(-48)\big)\\ &=207 \end{aligned}$$

737.stem:
Finn is working in the garden when he has an accident and puts a hole in the bottom of his rainwater tank. At the time of the accident, the tank contained 10 200 litres of water.

In the first hour after the accident, Finn noticed that the volume of water in the tank decreased by 200 litres.

In the second hour, he noticed that the volume of water in the tank decreased by a further 250 litres.

Finn is concerned that the leak is growing, but he is not sure what will happen next. He wonders if the amount of water leaking from the tank each hour might form an arithmetic sequence or geometric sequence.

parts.latex: If the amount of water that leaks out of the tank each hour forms an arithmetic sequence, how many hours will it take until the tank is empty?
If the amount of water that leaks out of the tank each hour forms a geometric sequence, show that eight hours after the leak, over 60% of the water remains in the tank

solutions.latex:
The leak each hour is arithmetic with $a = 200$, $d = 50$, and the tank is empty when $S_n = 10\,200$.

Using $S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right]$:
$$\begin{aligned} 10\,200 &= \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2(200) + (n-1) \times 50\right] \\ 20\,400 &= n(400 + 50n - 50) \\ 20\,400 &= 350n + 50n^2 \\ n^2 + 7n - 408 &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
Using the quadratic formula:
$$\begin{aligned} n &= \dfrac{-7 \pm \sqrt{7^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-408)}}{2} \\ &= -24 \text{ or } 17 \end{aligned}$$
$n > 0$, so $n = 17$.

$\therefore$ Tank empty after 17 hours.
criteria: Correct substitution into $S_n$, or equivalent merit

meta.concern: transcribed from handwritten solutions copy (images, no text layer)

solutions.latex:
The leak each hour is geometric with $a = 200$, $r = \dfrac{250}{200} = 1.25$, $n = 8$.

Using $S_n = \dfrac{a(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_8 &= \dfrac{200(1.25^8 - 1)}{1.25 - 1} \\ &= 3968.37 \text{ L has leaked out} \end{aligned}$$
$$10\,200 - 3968.37 = 6231.63 \text{ L}$$
$$\dfrac{6231.63}{10\,200} \times 100 = 61.09\%$$
$\therefore$ After 8 hours more than $60\%$ of water remains.
criteria: Correct substitution into $S_8$, or equivalent merit

829.stem: A company produces 40 tonnes of rice in the first year of production, 80 tonnes in the second year and 120 tonnes in its third year of production. The company continues to increase its rice production by this same amount each year thereafter.

parts.latex: In which year of production did the amount of rice produced for that year equal 2000 tonnes?
What was the total amount of rice produced in the first 20 years of production?

solutions.latex:
$40 + 80 + 120 + \ldots$ is an arithmetic sequence with $a = 40$, $d = 40$. Using $T_n = a + (n - 1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2000 &= 40 + (n - 1) \times 40 \\ n - 1 &= \dfrac{1960}{40} \\ &= 49 \\ n &= 50 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ In the 50th year.
criteria: Correct substitution into the formula or correct $n$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The first three terms of an arithmetic sequence are $x+6$, $2x-5$ and $4x-11$.

Find the value of $x$.

solutions.latex:
In an arithmetic sequence the common difference is constant, so $T_3-T_2=T_2-T_1$ (or $T_3+T_1=2T_2$):
$$\begin{aligned} 4x-11-(2x-5)&=2x-5-(x+6)\\ 4x-11-2x+5&=2x-5-x-6\\ 2x-6&=x-11\\ x&=-5 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Obtains the correct equation $T_3-T_2=T_2-T_1$, or equivalent merit

954.stem: A mum deposited \$100 into her son's saving account on his first birthday. She deposits \$125 on his second birthday. \$150 on his third birthday, and so on.

parts.latex: Calculate the amount of money she will deposit into her son's account on his 15th birthday.
On which birthday will the mum deposit \$700?
Hence, calculate the total amount she will have deposited over 25 years.

solutions.latex:
The deposits form an arithmetic sequence:
$$100,\ 125,\ 150,\ \ldots$$
$$a=100,\quad d=25$$
Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_{15}&=100+14\times 25\\ &=450\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ she deposits $\$450$ on his 15th birthday.
criteria: Makes a mistake in $a$ or $d$, leading to an incorrect result from a correct term calculation, or equivalent merit

meta.top_criterion_original: Correctly identified a and d and found $T_{15}$

solutions.latex:
Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$ with $T_n=700$:
$$\begin{aligned}100+25(n-1)&=700\\ 100+25n-25&=700\\ 25n&=625\\ n&=25\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ on his 25th birthday.
criteria: Uses the correct formula with an arithmetic mistake, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$, with the 25th deposit $\$700$ from part (b):
$$\begin{aligned}S_{25}&=\dfrac{25}{2}(100+700)\\ &=10000\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ she deposits $\$10\,000$ in total.
criteria: Uses the correct summation formula with an arithmetic mistake, or equivalent merit

meta.top_criterion_original: Correct summation formula with correct answer

parts.latex: If $y^2=(2m-y)\,(2n-y)$, show that $\dfrac{1}{m},\dfrac{1}{y},\dfrac{1}{n}$ (in this order) forms the terms of an arithmetic sequence.

solutions.latex:
Expanding and making $y$ the subject:
$$\begin{aligned}y^2&=(2m-y)(2n-y)\\ y^2&=4mn-2my-2ny+y^2\\ 2my+2ny&=4mn\\ y&=\dfrac{2mn}{m+n}\\ \dfrac{1}{y}&=\dfrac{m+n}{2mn}\end{aligned}$$
Checking $T_2-T_1$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_2-T_1&=\dfrac{1}{y}-\dfrac{1}{m}\\ &=\dfrac{m+n}{2mn}-\dfrac{1}{m}\cdot\dfrac{2n}{2n}\\ &=\dfrac{m+n-2n}{2mn}\\ &=\dfrac{m-n}{2mn}\end{aligned}$$
Checking $T_3-T_2$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_3-T_2&=\dfrac{1}{n}-\dfrac{1}{y}\\ &=\dfrac{1}{n}\cdot\dfrac{2m}{2m}-\dfrac{m+n}{2mn}\\ &=\dfrac{2m-m-n}{2mn}\\ &=\dfrac{m-n}{2mn}\\ &=T_2-T_1\end{aligned}$$
As $T_3-T_2=T_2-T_1$, the three terms form an arithmetic sequence.
criteria: Finds $T_3-T_2$ and $T_2-T_1$ in terms of $y$, $m$ and $n$, or equivalent merit
Expands the $y^2$ equation, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Note that students who automatically assumed $T_3-T_2=T_2-T_1$ can only receive 2 out of 3 marks maximum, as they assumed the terms were equal prior to showing the terms form an arithmetic sequence
meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the denominator of $T_2-T_1$ is $2mn$ (source printed $\dfrac{m+n-2n}{2n}=\dfrac{m-n}{2n}$).

figures.cap: three squares of sides 5 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm joined corner to corner in a staircase; NOT TO SCALE

parts.latex: What is the perimeter of the 24th square in this sequence?
Find the total perimeter of all the squares after the robot draws the 24th square.
The amount of ink in the robot's pen can only draw up to a maximum of 12 000 cm. How many complete squares can the robot draw using the one pen?

solutions.latex:
The side lengths form the arithmetic sequence $5, 8, 11, \ldots$ with first term $a=5$ and common difference $d=3$.

Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$ with $n=24$:
$$\begin{aligned} T_{24}&=5+(24-1)\times3\\ &=74 \end{aligned}$$
The side length of the 24th square is 74 cm, and its perimeter is 4 times the side length:
$$4\times74=296$$
$\therefore$ The perimeter of the 24th square is 296 cm.
criteria: Uses correct formula to get side length of 24th square but does not multiply by 4 to obtain perimeter, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The perimeter of the first square is $4\times5=20$ cm and the perimeter of the 24th square is 296 cm.

Using the arithmetic series formula $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{24}&=\dfrac{24}{2}(20+296)\\ &=3792 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ The total perimeter of the first 24 squares is 3792 cm.

12 000 cm is the total perimeter the robot can draw. Dividing by 4 gives the series in terms of side length instead of perimeter:
$$12\,000\div4=3000$$
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $S_n=3000$, $a=5$ and $d=3$:
$$\begin{aligned} 3000&=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2\times5+(n-1)3\big)\\ 6000&=n(10+3n-3)\\ 6000&=3n^2+7n\\ 0&=3n^2+7n-6000 \end{aligned}$$
Using the quadratic formula:
$$n=-45.9 \text{ or } n=43.6$$
$n>0$, so the negative answer is invalid.

1009.stem: The $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is given by $T_n=5n-3$.

parts.latex: Write down the first 3 terms of the sequence.
Find the sum of the first 50 terms.

solutions.latex:
Substituting $n=1,2,3$ into $T_n=5n-3$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_1&=5\times1-3=2\\T_2&=5\times2-3=7\\T_3&=5\times3-3=12\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the first 3 terms are $2,7,12$.

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$ with $a=2$, $d=5$, $n=50$:
$$\begin{aligned}S_{50}&=\dfrac{50}{2}\left[2\times2+(50-1)\times5\right]\\&=25\times(4+245)\\&=6225\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$, or into $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+\ell)$ with the correct 50th term, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Determine the last term under 100 in the sequence below.

$$-11,\quad-4,\quad3,\quad10,\quad17,\quad\ldots$$

solutions.latex:
The sequence is arithmetic with $a=-11$, $d=7$. Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_n&=-11+7(n-1)\\&=-11+7n-7\\&=7n-18\end{aligned}$$
For the terms under 100:
$$\begin{aligned}7n-18&<100\\7n&<118\\n&<16.857\ldots\end{aligned}$$
The largest whole number is $n=16$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_{16}&=7(16)-18\\&=94\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the last term under 100 is the 16th term, $94$.

parts.latex:
A toy racetrack consists of multiple track pieces which join together.

The first and longest piece of the track is 35 cm long, and each piece of track after the longest is 2 centimetres shorter than the previous piece.

The total length of the completed track is 2.6 metres.

Find the length of the shortest piece of track.

solutions.latex:
The track lengths form an arithmetic sequence with $a=35$, $d=-2$ and $S_n=260$ cm (2.6 m).

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2(35)+(n-1)(-2)\big)&=260\\n(70-2n+2)&=520\\n(72-2n)&=520\\72n-2n^2&=520\\2n^2-72n+520&=0\\n^2-36n+260&=0\\n&=\dfrac{36\pm\sqrt{36^2-4(1)(260)}}{2}\\&=26\text{ or }10\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}T_{26}&=35+(26-1)(-2)\\&=35+25(-2)\\&=-15\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
Lengths cannot be negative, so $n\ne26$.
$$\begin{aligned}T_{10}&=35+(10-1)(-2)\\&=17\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the length of the shortest piece is 17 cm.
criteria: Forms the correct equation $\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2(35)+(n-1)(-2)\big)=260$, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: The last mark is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $T_{26}=-15$ with a justification for rejecting it and $\dfrac{1}{2}$ for 17 cm. Generally done well; a few did not find the $T_n$ values or did not eliminate the negative $T_n$ with an appropriate justification.

parts.latex: What is the value of $\ln 2+2\ln 2+3\ln 2+\ldots+2n\ln 2$?

solutions.latex:
Taking out the common factor $\ln 2$ leaves an arithmetic series of $2n$ terms from $1$ to $2n$, summed with $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$:
$$\begin{aligned}\ln 2(1+2+3+\ldots+2n)&=\ln 2\left(\dfrac{2n}{2}(1+2n)\right)\\&=\ln 2\,\big(n(1+2n)\big)\\&=n(2n+1)\ln 2\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
The first and last terms of an arithmetic series are 10 and 60 respectively.

The sum of the series is 3535.

solutions.latex:
The first and last terms are known, so use $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\left[a+l\right]$:
$$\begin{aligned}3535&=\dfrac{n}{2}\left[10+60\right]\\7070&=n(70)\\n&=\dfrac{7070}{70}\\&=101\end{aligned}$$

The last term is $T_{101}=60$. Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned}60&=10+(101-1)d\\50&=100d\\d&=\dfrac{50}{100}\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$$
OR, as the 100 equal steps go from $10$ to $60$:
$$\begin{aligned}d&=\dfrac{60-10}{100}\\&=\dfrac{50}{100}\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following formulas could be used to calculate the sum of the first $n$ positive \textbf{even} numbers?

parts.latex: The sum of the first ten terms of an arithmetic sequence is $(-50)$.  The next ten terms of this sequence add to $(-450)$.  Find the first term and common difference of the sequence.

solutions.latex:
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $S_{10}=-50$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{10}{2}\big(2a+(10-1)d\big)&=-50\\5(2a+9d)&=-50\\2a+9d&=-10 &&(1)\end{aligned}$$
The first 20 terms add to $(-50)+(-450)=-500$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{20}{2}\big(2a+(20-1)d\big)&=-500\\10(2a+19d)&=-500\\2a+19d&=-50 &&(2)\end{aligned}$$
$(2)-(1)$:
$$\begin{aligned}10d&=-40\\d&=-4\end{aligned}$$
Substituting into (1):
$$\begin{aligned}2a+9(-4)&=-10\\2a&=26\\a&=13\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the first term is $13$ and the common difference is $-4$.

parts.latex: The arithmetic sequence $x, 2x+1, 4x-5$, is formed. What is the value of $x$?

parts.latex: Show that the sequence $\log 3,\log 9,\log 27,\log 81,\ldots$ is an arithmetic sequence.
Hence or otherwise find the sum to 10 terms of the sequence $\log 3,\log 9,\log 27,\log 81,\ldots$ Leave your answer in simplest exact form.

solutions.latex:
Using the log law $\log a^n=n\log a$:
$$\begin{aligned}&\log3,\log9,\log27,\log81,\ldots\\&=\log3,\log3^2,\log3^3,\log3^4,\ldots\\&=\log3,2\log3,3\log3,4\log3,\ldots\end{aligned}$$
Testing for a common difference:
$$\begin{aligned}T_2-T_1&=2\log3-\log3\\&=\log3\\T_3-T_2&=3\log3-2\log3\\&=\log3\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ AP where $a=\log3$, $d=\log3$
criteria: Correctly uses a log law OR finds $T_2-T_1$ and $T_3-T_2$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Seats in a theatre are arranged in rows. The number of seats in this theatre form the terms of an arithmetic series.

The sixth row has 23 seats, and the fifteenth row has 50 seats. If the theatre has 20 rows, how many seats are in the theatre?

solutions.latex:
Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$ with $T_6=23$ and $T_{15}=50$:
$$\begin{aligned}a+5d&=23\\a+14d&=50\end{aligned}$$
Solving simultaneously (subtract the first equation from the second):
$$\begin{aligned}9d&=27\\d&=3\\a&=8\end{aligned}$$
Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big[2a+(n-1)d\big]$:
$$\begin{aligned}S_{20}&=\dfrac{20}{2}\big[2\times 8+19\times 3\big]\\&=730\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ There are a total of 730 seats.
criteria: Correctly finds $a$ and $d$, or equivalent merit

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$:
$$\begin{aligned}S_{385}&=\dfrac{385}{2}(17+3089)\\ &=597\,905\end{aligned}$$

1332.stem: A gardener plants apple trees in rows, starting with a row of 14 trees. Each successive row has 6 more trees.

parts.latex: Calculate the number of trees in the $5^{\text{th}}$ row.
The gardener plants 6020 trees. How many rows are there?

solutions.latex:
$a=14$, $d=6$

Using $T_n=a+(n-1)d$:
$$\begin{aligned}T_5&=14+(5-1)6\\ &=38\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ 38 trees in $5^{\text{th}}$ row

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $a=14$, $d=6$, $S_n=6020$:
$$\begin{aligned}6020&=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2(14)+(n-1)6\big)\\ 12\,040&=n(28+6n-6)\\ 12\,040&=28n+6n^2-6n\\ 6n^2+22n-12\,040&=0\end{aligned}$$
Using the quadratic formula:
$$\begin{aligned}n&=\dfrac{-22\pm\sqrt{22^2-4(6)(-12\,040)}}{2(6)}\\ &=\dfrac{-22\pm\sqrt{289\,444}}{12}\\ &=\dfrac{-22\pm538}{12}\end{aligned}$$
$n>0$, so $n=43$.

$\therefore$ there are 43 rows.

parts.latex: In an arithmetic series, the sum of the first three terms is 21 and the sum of the first four terms is 36. What is the sum of the first five terms?

solutions.latex:
Using $S_3=21$ and $S_4=36$:
$$T_4=S_4-S_3=36-21=15$$
The sum of three terms of an arithmetic series is $3T_2$, so
$$\begin{aligned} 3T_2 &= 21 \\ T_2 &= 7 \end{aligned}$$
$T_4=T_2+2d$ gives $15=7+2d$, so $d=4$ and
$$T_5=T_4+d=19$$
$$S_5=S_4+T_5=36+19=55$$

parts.latex: Volodymyr likes Tic Tacs(R). On Monday he eats 2, on Tuesday he eats 4, on Wednesday he eats 6, and so on in this patern. After how many days will he have eaten a total of 132 Tic Tacs ?

solutions.latex:
The days form an arithmetic series $2,4,6,8,\ldots$ with $a=2$ and $d=2$.

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $S_n=132$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{n}{2}(4+2n-2) &= 132 \\ \dfrac{n}{2}(2+2n) &= 132 \\ n(1+n) &= 132 \\ n^2+n-132 &= 0 \\ (n+12)(n-11) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
$n=-12$ or $n=11$, and $n>0$.
$$\therefore\ n=11 \text{ days}$$

This is an arithmetic sequence with $a=\log_2 3$ and $d=\log_2 3$:

parts.latex:
An arithmetic and geometric sequence both have first term 1, and their second terms are equal.

The 14$^{\text{th}}$ term of the arithmetic sequence is three times the third term of the geometric sequence.

Given that both sequences contain only integers, find the common ratio and common difference for each sequence.

solutions.latex:
The arithmetic sequence is $1,\ 1+d,\ 1+2d,\ \ldots$ and the geometric sequence is $1,\ r,\ r^2,\ \ldots$

The second terms are equal, so $r=1+d$.

The $14^{\text{th}}$ term of the arithmetic sequence is $1+13d$, and the $3^{\text{rd}}$ term of the geometric sequence is $r^2$, so $1+13d=3r^2$.

Substitute $r=1+d$:
$$\begin{aligned} 1+13d &= 3(1+d)^2 \\ 1+13d &= 3+6d+3d^2 \\ 3d^2-7d+2 &= 0 \\ (3d-1)(d-2) &= 0 \\ d &= \dfrac{1}{3}\text{ or }2 \end{aligned}$$
If $d=\dfrac{1}{3}$, the arithmetic sequence has non-integer terms (for example the second term is $\dfrac{4}{3}$), so $d=2$, and $r=1+2=3$.
$$\therefore\ \text{arithmetic: }d=2;\quad\text{geometric: }r=3$$
criteria: Solves simultaneously to obtain the two values of $r$ or $d$
Correctly uses one of the sequence formulas, for example obtains $T_2=1+d$

parts.latex: Find the $30^{\text{th}}$ term in the sequence $-8,\,-2,\,4\,\ldots$

solutions.latex:
The sequence is arithmetic with $a=-8$ and $d=-2-(-8)=6$.
$$\begin{aligned}T_{30}&=a+(30-1)d \\ &=-8+29\times 6 \\ &=166\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A series has following terms:

$2+5+8+11+14+17+\ldots$

What is the sum of the first 30 terms of the series

solutions.latex:
The terms increase by $3$ each time, so this is an arithmetic series with $a=2$ and $d=3$.

Using $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ with $n=30$:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{30} &= \dfrac{30}{2}\big(2(2)+29(3)\big) \\ &= 15\times 91 \\ &= 1365 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Consider the series $\log_a 54+\log_a 18+\log_a 6+\ldots\ldots\ldots\ldots$

Which of the following statements best describe the series?

solutions.latex:
Find the differences between consecutive terms:
$$\begin{aligned}\log_a 18-\log_a 54&=\log_a\dfrac{18}{54}=\log_a 3^{-1}=-\log_a 3 \\ \log_a 6-\log_a 18&=\log_a\dfrac{6}{18}=\log_a 3^{-1}=-\log_a 3\end{aligned}$$
The differences are constant, so the series is arithmetic with common difference $-\log_a 3$.

1956.stem: Madison is learning to drive. Her first lesson is 10 minutes long. Her second lesson is 15 minutes long. Each subsequent lesson is 5 minutes longer than the previous lesson.

parts.latex: How long will Madison's fifteenth lesson be?
How many hours of lessons will Madison have completed after her fifteenth lesson?
During which lesson will Madison have completed a total of 40 hours of driving lessons?

solutions.latex:
The lesson lengths $10+15+20+25+\ldots$ form an arithmetic series with first term $a=10$ and common difference $d=5$.
$$\begin{aligned}T_{15}&=a+(15-1)d\\ &=10+14\times5\\ &=80\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$

Use the sum of an arithmetic series, $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a+(n-1)d\right]$, with $a=10$, $d=5$:
$$\begin{aligned}S_{15}&=\dfrac{15}{2}\left[2(10)+(15-1)\cdot5\right]\\ &=\dfrac{15}{2}\cdot90\\ &=675\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$
Convert to hours: $675\div60=11.25$.
$$\therefore\ 11.25\text{ hours}=11\text{ hours }15\text{ minutes}$$

$40$ hours $=40\times60=2400$ minutes. Find $n$ with $S_n=2400$:
$$\begin{aligned}2400&=\dfrac{n}{2}\left[2(10)+(n-1)\cdot5\right]\\ 4800&=n(15+5n)\\ 5n^2+15n-4800&=0\\ n^2+3n-960&=0\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}n&=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{3^2-4(1)(-960)}}{2}\\ &=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{3849}}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Since $n>0$, $n=\dfrac{-3+\sqrt{3849}}{2}\approx29.5$.

Check with whole lessons: $S_{29}=2320<2400$ and $S_{30}=2475>2400$.
$$\therefore\ \text{Madison completes 40 hours during her 30th lesson}$$
